title: Attention kernel gated startup regulator
creator: Sofia Jensen
description:
Problem: After the rollout of FA3-optimized kernels and a new microbatching heuristic, a subset of production prefill workloads show oscillating kernel choices across warmup iterations, causing 15-30% latency variance and occasional OOMs during cold-start heavy traffic. The behaviour seems tied to early-prefill profiling and aggressive 'best kernel' scoring that flips between v2 and v3 variants as sequence-length distributions change during the first 5 requests.

Goal: Implement a gated startup regulator that stabilizes kernel selection during the prefill -> decode transition window. The regulator should bias decisions to conservative, high-memory-safety kernels for the first N warmup cycles, ramp to higher-throughput kernels based on verified stability signals (memory slack, steady latency, absence of soft OOM warnings). This should reduce startup jitter and avoid regression cases while preserving throughput after steady-state is reached.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 95th-percentile latency variance in simulated cold-start traces reduced by >=50% versus current canary; 2) No increase in steady-state median latency >5% after regulator ramp; 3) No reproducible OOMs in stress harness across 10k cold-start sequences; 4) Automated canary telemetry emits gating decisions and ramp metrics.
technical_notes:
Design: Add a 'startup regulator' layer into the kernel selector pipeline that consumes runtime signals: recent kernel success/failure, observed workspace allocation headroom, rolling median latency for the request route, and microbatch size history. The regulator exposes a simple state machine: PROBE -> HOLD -> RAMP.

- PROBE (first 1-3 requests): pick conservative kernel but allow a single speculative high-throughput probe per N requests. Log probe outcome.
- HOLD: when probes indicate instability (OOMs or >x% latency spike), keep using conservative choices and increase probe cooldown.
- RAMP: after M successful probes with stable metrics, widen kernel candidate set to include FA3 aggressive kernels and reduce probe cooldown.

Tuning knobs: PROBE_COUNT, SUCCESS_WINDOW, MEMORY_MARGIN_BYTES, LATENCY_STABILITY_THRESHOLD_MS. Default: PROBE_COUNT=3, SUCCESS_WINDOW=8, MEMORY_MARGIN_BYTES=50MB, LATENCY_STABILITY_THRESHOLD_MS=10ms.

Integration points: kernel_selector_v2 and kernel_selector_v3 adapters; prefill scheduler should expose per-request metric hooks; runtime telemetry path needs a new gating decision event type.

Fallback behaviour: If MemoryMargin breached or soft OOMs seen, immediately fallback to last-known-conservative kernel and mark route as 'degraded' for 30s.

Compatibility: Works with both FlashAttention v2 and v3 kernels, quantized and non-quantized variants. Will avoid changing model artifact format.

Risks: too conservative defaults may delay throughput gains; too aggressive probing may reintroduce regression; complexity increases selector maintenance burden.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature branch with unit tests and deterministic harness (local); 2) Integration tests in canary cluster with synthetic cold-start trace set A; 3) Internal dogfood on low-traffic tenant for 48h; 4) Gradual rollout to 10% of routes for 1 day, 50% for 2 days, full rollout if metrics stable.

Telemetry/observability: add gating_decision.{route,kernel,decision,reason,probe_result,mem_headroom,latency_ms} metrics and a dashboard showing regulator state over time. Alerts: gating_fallback_rate > 2% for 1h.
measurements: Planned measurements: p50/p95/p99 latency prefill and decode windows, kernel_choice_entropy (how often kernel flips in first 10 requests), workspace_peak_mb, soft_oom_count, successful_probe_rate. Baseline collected from canary on 2026-02-10-16:00 UTC. Expected improvement: kernel_choice_entropy -60%, p95 variance -50%.
